title: A large singleton Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Then some coordinate $i$ has singleton Fourier coefficient at least $\dfrac{9\cdot 9^{-T}}{T^2}$, where $T$ is the total influence of $f$ divided by its variance.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
